a_cheaper_option_declined_because_it_fla.option: restrict to the first 553 feature columns (the v1 set), roughly halving memory
a_cheaper_option_declined_because_it_fla.why_declined: The cheaper feature set produces a LARGER frozen-set margin, and it does so by WEAKENING the baselines rather than by improving the model. Adopting it after two OOM kills would have been choosing the option that flatters the study under cover of a resource constraint. The memory problem was solved on the full 1108-column set instead. Recorded because the decision went against this study's interest and would otherwise be invisible.

byte_model_0009_training_trace.reading_1_it_converged_rather_than_ran_o: The real-label loss falls 3.2587 -> 3.0877 and flattens: the last five epochs move 0.0145 in total, under 0.005 per epoch. So this is a model that converged to a poor solution, not one truncated mid-descent. That makes the negative stronger than a simple 'we ran out of compute'.
byte_model_0009_training_trace.reading_2_the_null_control_is_ALSO_evide: The shuffled-label loss never moves from ln(26) at all - 0.0006 across ten epochs. That is a clean null control, and it is simultaneously evidence that this architecture cannot memorise 100000 random labels. A model with no capacity to overfit may simply be too small, so part of 'it failed' is 'it was small'. This confound is real and is stated rather than left implicit.
byte_model_0009_training_trace.status: transcribed from the 0009 run log so the loss trajectory is checkable, not asserted

eval_protocol: grouped by source chunk throughout; 26 classes; chance 0.0385; n_train 100000; n_eval 26000; baselines trained on the SAME data as the model

failed_hypotheses.hypothesis: DEFLATE is bit-packed, so Huffman codes do not respect byte boundaries and a byte-aligned histogram of entropy-coded data is near-uniform by construction. Reading the fragment at all 8 bit alignments and taking entropy, chi-square, top-1 and top-5 mass and support per alignment - 40 features - plus a stored-block LEN/NLEN complement detector, should expose structure the byte-aligned view cannot see.
failed_hypotheses.kept: Yes. The 43 features are retained because they cost 0.14 ms per fragment and are not harmful, but they are recorded as having earned nothing.
failed_hypotheses.verdict: NO IMPROVEMENT. RandomForest went slightly DOWN (0.1543 -> 0.1506) and HGB moved 0.1482 -> 0.1485, inside noise. The hypothesis as implemented is not supported.
failed_hypotheses.what_it_suggests: All four model classes cluster at 0.13-0.15 regardless of features, which is the signature of a FEATURE ceiling rather than a model problem. Either the bit-alignment idea is wrong, or five summary statistics per alignment discard exactly the shape that matters - which is what v3 tests by keeping the histograms instead of summarising them.

candidates.mlp: 0.0913 at n=20000 - clearly the wrong class here

model_selection.honest_caveat: If HGB does NOT overtake RF at the top rung, this choice cost the study accuracy, and that will be visible because both curves are recorded here.
model_selection.reasoning: RandomForest is better at every size measured, but it is rising at roughly +0.021 per decade against HGB's +0.029, and the gap has already narrowed from 0.0151 at n=10^4 to 0.0072 at n=10^5. For a SCALING study the steeper model is the right instrument, not the one that happens to lead at a tenth of target scale. HGB is also histogram-based and fits in memory at 10^6 where a RandomForest with 150 unpruned trees would not. The choice is recorded here and written into every artifact as model_class so it cannot be revisited silently.

open_question: Every number above is measured at n=10^5. The preregistered margin clause is evaluated at the TOP RUNG, and the study is specified to 10^6. The margin has therefore NOT yet been tested at the scale the thesis is about. The baselines are capacity-limited and will saturate; the model is not. Whether that opens the margin is the actual experiment.

permutation_p_is_at_its_floor.why: An exact permutation test over 4 rungs has 4! = 24 orderings, so the smallest attainable p-value is 1/24. The reported p IS that floor. It therefore says the observed ordering is the most extreme of the 24 possible; it does NOT say p could have been smaller with the same data. Any reading of it as 'just under 0.05' is wrong - more rungs, not a better result, is what would lower it.

top_rung_was_set_by_memory_not_by_result.oom_history: Six attempts. Five were killed at a ~13.9 GB ceiling. The dominant cause was found only on the fifth: np.load(path, mmap_mode='r') SILENTLY IGNORES mmap_mode for a .npz, so the 5.76 GB corpus that the code claimed to be memory-mapping was fully resident the whole time. Secondary cause, real but smaller: sklearn's HGB uses X_DTYPE=float64 and silently widens a float32 pool, then its internal train_test_split copies it again. Fixed by mapping the STORED zip entry in place (tools/pivot/npzmap.py), gathering rows chunkwise in ascending source order, widening to float64 up front, passing an explicit validation set, and holding the evaluation block at float32 with per-chunk widening. Peak 11.69 GB, as projected.
top_rung_was_set_by_memory_not_by_result.why: The top rung is 800,000 of the 1,040,000 training fragments available after the grouped split. The cap was NOT chosen for its accuracy - it was set during OOM debugging, before any 800,000-fragment number existed, and the run that produced it was the first one to survive. 1k->800k is 2.9031 decades, above the preregistered 2.0, so the frozen scope is met without the cap doing any work for the verdict.

why: Model and feature choices for the scaled run are made ONCE on pilot data and then held fixed. This records every choice and every FAILED hypothesis, so the selection cannot be quietly re-run after seeing a number, and so a hypothesis that did not work does not vanish because it was inconvenient.

why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.finding_1_nothing_collapses_differential: Every subset degrades by almost exactly the same factor from 4096 to 1024: the 1024/4096 accuracy ratio runs 0.589 to 0.628 across six subsets, a spread of 0.04. There is no family that survives the shorter window and no family that dies in it. The ENTIRE representation degrades uniformly, which is what one expects if every feature is a statistical estimate over the window and a quarter of the bytes makes every estimate worse by a similar factor.
why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.finding_2_the_alignment_features_never_e: Dropping all 555 alignment features costs 0.0099 at 4096 and 0.0016 at 1024. The v2 alignment SUMMARIES were already recorded in this log as having earned nothing; this extends that verdict to v3's alignment HISTOGRAMS, which were built on the hypothesis that summarising was the problem. It was not the problem. Roughly half the feature vector buys about one accuracy point at the window where the study works, and near-nothing at the window where it does not.
why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.not_quotable_as: evidence about the world. It is an engineering measurement about this repository's own feature set, and any fix it might suggest needs its own preregistration frozen before measurement.
why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.prior_recorded_before_the_run: Written into the commit that launched it: 'the 512 alignment-histogram columns are the casualty - at a quarter of the bytes each bin holds a quarter of the counts'. THAT PRIOR WAS WRONG, and it was wrong in a way worth recording: the alignment histograms are not what dies at 1024, because they were never carrying much at 4096 either.
why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.status: DIAGNOSTIC, not preregistered. Run after 0007 returned CARVE_FAILS, to ask whether the failure sits in one repairable part of the representation.
why_1024_fails_is_not_localised.what_this_means_for_a_fix: There is no repairable component to repair. A model that works at 1024 would need a different KIND of representation - learning from the raw bit sequence rather than from summary statistics over it - not a mended feature family. That is a materially larger project than the one this diagnostic was run to scope, and it is NOT started here. It also re-reads the transfer collapse: the 4096-trained model does not fail at 1024 because one family shifted, but because every feature is a window-length-dependent statistic, so the joint distribution is systematically different rather than noisier.
